android.desc:
Find a trail worth taking, then bring the map with you. Hedda Maps helps you explore mountain terrain in 3D, plan a hike and keep your map ready when mobile data is gone.

Plan your hike
Explore satellite imagery and 3D terrain to understand ridges, valleys and approaches before you leave. Turn trails, peaks, huts, shelters, mountain passes, campsites, natural attractions and other map layers on or off.

Tap a destination to highlight a mapped route when one is available. If there are several options, switch between them and compare distance, ascent and steepness. Planning from home? Double-tap the map to set a simulated GPS position and preview routes from that point.

Routes and points of interest come from available OpenStreetMap data.

Take it offline
Download a map to your phone before the hike. You can view it and use your device's real GPS to see your position without a mobile data connection. Creating and downloading new maps requires internet access.

Explore more places
Start with included Romanian mountain maps, or browse the free map library for places across Europe and beyond. Want a different area? Choose a rectangular region anywhere in the world and request a custom map. You can keep using the app while your map is being prepared.

On the free plan, you can create one custom map per week up to 16 x 16 km. Premium gives you more custom map creation and high-resolution imagery (Romania only for now, more regions will be added in time).

Pick a mountain, open a free map and start planning your next hike.

quotes.text:
Hi,

This is my first post although I have been following Hacker News for years.

I have been building something similar except not for Minecraft but hiking maps on mobile (Android). This is my app: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.chessvortexgames.maps

I combine OpenStreetMap data for routes, satellite data from Sentinel-2 and Copernicus DEM GLO-30 for heights, resolution is around 10m/pixel for image and 30m for heights - those are the highest resolution datasets I can legally redistribute, although I am also including what I call hi-res maps building for some countries (USA, France, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, Romania) which has image resolution at 1.5m/pixel instead of 10m.

I could have used higher resolution for hi-res maps, data is available at precision like 30-50cm/pixel but this being a mobile app I needed to consider storage for a map on mobile, at hi-res a 10x10 km squared area takes around 25MB.

The idea for this came from my own hiking trips, in many mountains there is not so good internet connection, so I can build an offline map beforehand and in terrain I can use this to see where I am in 3D - and just use the phone GPS for location, no data needed.

For building the map packages I have setup a linux server that combines all 3 data sources (OpenStreetMap, Sentinel-2, Copernicus GLO-30) so once an area is chosen it can build it in like 1-3 minutes. Since all OSM endpoints are giving lots of timeouts I setup a local OSM mirror with the data …
